{"content": "This is the core tension. Relying on verified GitHub PR artifacts (E) paired with complexity (C) and impact (I) is technically robust, but compensation is high-stakes. To trust this, you need transparent, immutable audit trails. If you can prove the scoring model isn't being gamed by PR splitting or trivial commits\u2014perhaps by incorporating a senior-level override or weighted peer-review input\u2014it becomes significantly more viable for senior leadership. The tamper-proof PostgreSQL ledger is a step in the right direction for accountability.", "comment_id": 1}

{"content": "This 'Volt' system sounds like a recipe for disaster. Any metric based on 'verified output' or 'AI scoring' is just begging to be gamed by people who know how to write flashy commit messages while ignoring actual technical debt. Compensation should not be tied to a 'mathematical impact score' that engineers will inevitably spend more time optimizing than actually fixing core distributed bugs. Have you considered that the best engineers often produce the least 'measurable' impact until a major incident happens? Adding a 'senior-level override' just introduces political bias on top of flawed automation.", "comment_id": 5}

{"content": "I have evaluated systems like this throughout my career. By codifying complexity into a mathematical decay curve (e.g., C^1.4), you are incentivizing the appearance of activity over structural engineering integrity.
